Purpose and exclusions

Crafting consumes a validated recipe's resources and produces deterministic output in one durable operation. Blacksmithing, Alchemy, Cooking and Tailoring start as templates with separate profession progression and learned recipe sets.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create four profession definitions and station tags: Forge/Blacksmithing, AlchemyBench/Alchemy, Cookfire/Cooking, Loom/Tailoring.
  2. Author DA_Recipe_IronHatchet, DA_Recipe_HealingDraught, DA_Recipe_GrilledDace and DA_Recipe_WovenCloak with fixed outputs. Cooking input can come from the development fixture/vendor before fishing Phase 14; replace that sourcing path in the integrated loop afterward.
  3. Place BP_CraftingStation at Hearthford forge with StationId and tag; attach interaction interface only, not character inventory.
  4. Build WBP_Crafting with recipe filters, learned/locked state, ingredient counts, result tooltip, quantity and confirm/cancel. Bind counts to current inventory revision.
  5. Reopen gathering/loot/vendor catalogs so each ingredient has a real source. Add native component to authorized player command route and connect backend atomic command endpoint.
  6. Create delayed-after-commit and disconnect-before-completion service fixtures; rejoin L_Thornweald to verify exactly-one output.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Recipes, professions, stations and deterministic results. Rule owner: URPGCraftingComponent. This asset’s role is Crafting consumes a validated recipe's resources and produces deterministic output in one durable operation. Blacksmithing, Alchemy, Cooking and Tailoring start as templates with separate profession progression and learned recipe sets.

  1. At Station_Forge the player selects IronHatchet. UI previews 4 CopperOre, 2 AshLog and 25 currency, required Blacksmithing level 1 and deterministic one-hatchet output.
  2. Server verifies interaction, learned recipe, profession/tool/station gates, batch bound and alive/action state; it starts the authored craft duration without consuming materials yet.
  3. On completion revalidate current ingredients and output capacity using one planned transaction, including space freed by consumed stacks.
  4. Backend locks character inventory/wallet/profession/recipe records, consumes exact materials/currency, creates one gear UUID, adds profession XP and receipt together.
  5. Return committed output identity and revisions. PaperZD/tool/VFX cues observe success; no animation notify calls material consumption or output grant.
  6. Disconnect immediately after confirm or commit: unresolved action cancels under policy, but committed receipt remains. On another zone login, load the one hatchet and consumed inputs without replaying the recipe.
  7. Repeat-craft requests use separate bounded commands after prior receipt or an explicitly atomic batch; never an unbounded client loop.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Station_Forge / Recipe_IronHatchet / Character_A. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Missing materials/profession/recipe -> explicit reason, no consumption.
Two crafts compete for same ore -> only valid serialized outcome commits; no negative materials.
Output does not fit after planned consumption -> NoSpace and no input/currency loss.
Disconnect after commit -> one output on reconnect; retry returns same UUID.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
